c1-1b-001.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | What are you doing with that tape measure? I ___ the kitchen for the new cupboards. (measure) |

item.q: What are you doing with that tape measure? I ___ the kitchen for the new cupboards. (measure)
item.why: *measure* here is an action happening now (using a tape measure): present continuous, *I'm measuring*.
item.why_lv: *measure te* ir darbība, kas notiek tagad (mēra ar mērlenti): Present Continuous, *I'm measuring.*

c1-1b-002.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Our kitchen is tiny: it ___ only three metres by four. (measure) |

item.q: Our kitchen is tiny: it ___ only three metres by four. (measure)
item.why: *measure* here gives the size, a state: present simple, *it measures*. The continuous is used only for the action of measuring.
item.why_lv: *measure te* norāda izmēru, tas ir stāvoklis: Present Simple, *it measures*. Ilgstošo formu lieto *tikai* darbībai (kāds mēra).

c1-1b-003.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | We're eating out all week because they ___ a new kitchen in our flat. (fit) |

item.q: We're eating out all week because they ___ a new kitchen in our flat. (fit)
item.why: *fit* here means install, an action that is going on this week: present continuous, *they're fitting*. In the state meaning (*The jacket fits you*) it is simple.
item.why_lv: *fit te* nozīmē uzstādīt, darbība, kas notiek šonedēļ: Present Continuous, *they're fitting*. Stāvokļa nozīmē (*The jacket fits you*) lieto vienkāršo formu.

c1-1b-004.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Write one word in each gap: Why ___ you ___ so difficult about this? It's only a small change. |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: Why ___ you ___ so difficult about this? It's only a small change.
item.why: *be* in the continuous (*are being*) describes how someone is behaving now, not what they are like: *Why are you being so difficult?* = why are you acting like this?
item.why_lv: *be* ilgstošajā formā (*are being*) apraksta, kā kāds *uzvedas* tagad, nevis kāds viņš ir: *Why are you being so difficult?* = kāpēc *tu* tagad tā *uzvedies*?

c1-1b-005.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | It's nearly ten o'clock. I ___ the pharmacy is still open, but we can try. (doubt) |

item.q: It's nearly ten o'clock. I ___ the pharmacy is still open, but we can try. (doubt)
item.why: *doubt* is a state of mind and is rarely continuous: *I doubt the pharmacy is still open*.
item.why_lv: *doubt* ir domāšanas stāvoklis, un ilgstošo formu gandrīz nelieto: *I doubt the pharmacy is still open.*

c1-1b-006.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | My manager ___ taking early retirement, but she hasn't made up her mind yet. (consider) |

item.q: My manager ___ taking early retirement, but she hasn't made up her mind yet. (consider)
item.why: *consider* in the meaning *think carefully about* is only used in the continuous: *she's considering taking early retirement*.
item.why_lv: *consider* nozīmē rūpīgi apsvērt lieto *tikai* ilgstošajā formā: *she's considering taking early retirement*.

c1-1b-007.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | OK, I ___ you now. I'm sorry I didn't take your story seriously. (believe) |

item.q: OK, I ___ you now. I'm sorry I didn't take your story seriously. (believe)
item.why: *believe* stays in the present simple, also with *now*: *I believe you now*, not *I'm believing you now*.
item.why_lv: *believe* paliek Present Simple arī ar *now*: *I believe you now*, nevis *I'm believing you now.*

c1-1b-008.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | He considers taking early retirement next year.

key.correct: He considers taking early retirement next year.
wrong: I'm finding the new routine quite tiring.
I suggest you book a table in advance.
This dress doesn't fit me any more.

item.why: *consider* meaning *think about doing* is continuous: *He's considering taking early retirement*. *I'm finding* (a new impression), *I suggest* (the act of suggesting) and *doesn't fit* (a state) are correct.
item.why_lv: *consider* nozīmē apsvērt lieto ilgstošajā formā: *He's considering taking early retirement.* *I'm finding* (jauns *iespaids*), *I suggest* (*ieteikums* ar pašiem vārdiem) un *doesn't fit* (stāvoklis) ir *pareizi*.
item.correct: He considers taking early retirement next year.
wrong: I'm finding the new routine quite tiring.
I suggest you book a table in advance.
This dress doesn't fit me any more.

c1-1b-009.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | text | Answer with *constantly* and *change your mind*: "Actually, I'll have the fish, not the pasta." |

accepted: You are constantly changing your mind.

item.q: Answer with *constantly* and *change your mind*: "Actually, I'll have the fish, not the pasta."
item.why: *be constantly* + *-ing* shows that something happens so often that it is typical of the person, often with irritation: *You're constantly changing your mind.*
item.why_lv: *be constantly + -ing* rāda, ka kaut kas notiek tik bieži, ka tas ir raksturīgi cilvēkam, bieži ar *nepatiku*: *You're constantly changing your mind.*
answers: You are constantly changing your mind.

c1-1b-010.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Don't phone me at half past eight: I ___ usually ___ to work then. (drive) |

item.q: Don't phone me at half past eight: I ___ usually ___ to work then. (drive)
item.why: *usually* + present continuous: something we regularly do that is in progress at that time (*I'm usually driving to work then*).
item.why_lv: *usually* + Present Continuous: *ierasta* darbība, kas tajā laikā jau notiek (*I'm usually driving to work then*).

c1-1b-011.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.

key.correct: My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.
wrong: He's always offering to help with the shopping.
At eight I'm usually driving to work.
She constantly checks her phone in meetings.

item.why: *forever*, *always*, *constantly* go after *is*: *My neighbour is forever borrowing my tools.*
item.why_lv: *forever, always, constantly* stāv aiz *is*: *My neighbour is forever borrowing my tools.*
item.correct: My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.
wrong: He's always offering to help with the shopping.
At eight I'm usually driving to work.
She constantly checks her phone in meetings.

c1-1b-012.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | order | Put the words in order. | you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking

key.sentence: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
also: when I'm speaking you're constantly interrupting me

item.why: *constantly* goes between *you're* and the *-ing* form; the *when*-part can come first or second.
item.why_lv: *constantly* stāv starp *you're* un *-ing* formu; daļa ar *when* var būt pirmā vai otrā.
item.sentence: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
answers: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
when I'm speaking you're constantly interrupting me
